country_code.description: Keep only this `Country Code` (ISO alpha-2, or `FV` for fishing vessels). Pattern: ^[A-Za-z]{2}$.

cursor.description: Opaque continuation from a previous page's `next_cursor`. Pinned to the CSV URL and SHA-256 it was issued for; a moved publication fails with issue code `publication_changed`.

industry.description: Keep only rows whose `Industry` equals this value, case-insensitively.

limit.description:
Rows per page (the whole file is about 70 rows).

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 200; default 100.

order_type.description:
Keep only this `WRO/Finding` value.

Provider reference: allowed values ["WRO", "Finding"].

query.description: Case-insensitive substring match over entity, merchandise, country and remarks.

status.description: Keep only rows whose `Status` equals this value, case-insensitively (`Active`, `Partially Modified`, `Inactive-Pending Litigation`).

year.description:
Keep only rows with this `Calendar Year`.

Provider reference: minimum 1900; maximum 2100.

200.description:
The full current WRO and Findings list in file order (chronological), paginated by offset with a cursor pinned to one publication (CSV URL plus SHA-256). Every page re-resolves the CSV from the dataset page and re-fetches it; if the publication moved since the cursor was issued the call fails with `invalid_input` and issue code `publication_changed` instead of mixing versions. Filters narrow the list; pass the same filters with the cursor. No `records/changes`: CBP publishes no deltas, and revoked orders drop out of the file rather than change status, so keep history by diffing snapshots.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `records` as the primary payload key.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `aliases` | string[] | Alternative names from the `Entity` column, one per ` a/k/a ` segment after the first. Empty when the entity has none. |
| `calendar_year` | number | The `Calendar Year` column as published. |
| `country` | string | The `Country` column, e.g. `Fishing Vessels` for `FV`. |
| `country_code` | string | The `Country Code` column: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, or the pseudo-code `FV` for fishing vessels. |
| `effective_date` | string | The `Effective Date` column (M/D/YYYY in the file) as an ISO date. |
| `industry` | string | The `Industry` column, or null when the file leaves it blank. `All` is a published value. |
| `manufacturer` | string | The primary name in the `Entity` column (the text before the first ` a/k/a `). Some rows name a region, a sector (`Artisanal`) or a vessel rather than a company; it is never inferred from the merchandise. |
| `merchandise` | string | The `Merchandise` column. |
| `notice_url` | string | The `Press Release` column (a CBP or Federal Register URL), or null when blank. |
| `order_type` | string | The `WRO/Finding` column: `WRO` (Withhold Release Order) or `Finding`. |
| `publication_id` | string | The CSV filename, e.g. `withhold-release-orders-findings-fy26-2026-09-29.csv`; it changes with every dataset update. |
| `raw` | object | The identity tuple exactly as published (before whitespace normalisation and alias splitting). |
| `remarks` | string | The `Remarks` column (Treasury Decision and Federal Register citations, cross-references), or null when blank. |
| `retrieved_at` | string | When this program fetched the CSV (UTC). |
| `source_record_id` | string | Derived id: `wro:` + the first 16 hex characters of SHA-256 over `Effective Date\|WRO/Finding\|Entity\|Merchandise` (whitespace in each field collapsed to single spaces). The CSV has no id column; the tuple is unique across the file. |
| `source_url` | string | The dated CSV this row was read from. |
| `status` | string | The `Status` column exactly as published (`Active`, `Partially Modified`, `Inactive-Pending Litigation`, ...). Revoked orders drop out of the file rather than change status. |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

200.description:
Cheap version check of the WRO and Findings dataset: resolves the current dated CSV from the dataset page (the filename changes with every update), returns its URL, the page's `Last Modified` date, the file's HTTP Last-Modified and ETag, byte size, SHA-256 of the raw bytes, the column names and the row count.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `columns` | string[] | Header names in file order (the order changed between the June and September 2026 files; the program maps by name and requires the 11 known columns). |
| `data_dictionary_url` | string | The data dictionary PDF linked from the page, or null when no PDF is linked. |
| `dataset_url` | string | The dataset page the CSV was resolved from. |
| `etag` | string | The CSV response's `ETag` header verbatim (Apache `"<size-hex>-<mtime>"`), or null when absent. |
| `file_last_modified` | string | The CSV response's `Last-Modified` header verbatim, or null when absent. |
| `file_url` | string |  |
| `observed_at_ms` | number |  |
| `page_last_modified` | string | The page's `Last Modified` text verbatim (`Sep 29, 2026`), or null when the block is absent. |
| `publication_id` | string | The CSV filename, e.g. `withhold-release-orders-findings-fy26-2026-09-29.csv`. |
| `published_at` | string | The dataset page's `Last Modified: Mon D, YYYY` text as an ISO date; when the page omits it, the date embedded in the CSV filename. |
| `record_count` | number | Data rows in the CSV. |
| `retrieved_at` | string |  |
| `sha256` | string | SHA-256 of the raw CSV bytes (the publisher posts no hash). |
| `size_bytes` | number | Raw CSV byte count. |
